Wiring outlet, it can be simple, yes. Follow safety, always. If unsure or situation complicated, best to ask licensed electrician. They understand local code, laws. 

Tools and materials needed:

- Outlet, right amperage

Steps for new outlet installation:

1. Turn off power to circuit you work on, switch off breaker. 
2. Find nearby junction box, check with non-contact voltage detector for power. 
3. Safe now? Remove cover plate. 
4. Run new length of Romex from junction box to new outlet location. Drill holes through studs, floors, cut wall if needed. 
5. If old outlet has unused connection screws, attach new wire there to power new outlet. Label usually “load.” If not, detach existing wiring, combine colors, black to black, white to white, use pigtails to run single wire to outlet. 
6. Follow same steps for connecting wire to new outlet below for existing outlet. 
7. At new location, cut hole in wall for outlet. 
8. Attach electrical box, old-work type, to wall with screws, tension box tabs, secure place.

Steps for new outlet installation and replacing existing outlets:

1. Strip outer insulation from cable, separate wires. 
2. Strip about ½ inch insulation from each wire, black, white, green or bare. You may have 4th gray wire or red wire instead of black. Gray wire often needed for smart devices. Consult electrician if device needs it and no gray wire. Red wire means outlet switched, also “hot” like black wire. Commonly routed to lights or fans. 
3. Connect black wire to brass screw on outlet, “line,” tighten screw. This wire “hot,” carries current. 
4. Connect white wire to silver screw on outlet, “line,” tighten screw. This wire “neutral,” completes circuit. 
5. Connect green or bare wire to green screw on outlet, tighten screw. This wire “ground,” safely flows electricity to ground if short circuit. 
6. Gently push outlet into box, do not pinch wires. 
7. Screw outlet into box. 
8. Install cover plate. 
9. Turn power back on, test outlet, make sure working.
